clue.text: Top diamond geezer comes first

indicators.note: the geezer is placed ahead of the diamond in the assembled word

parts.note: a bod is slang for a person or chap, like geezer
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A gem of a bloke takes precedence over everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top diamond geezer' reads as praise for a great bloke (British slang 'diamond geezer'), but 'Top' is the definition: a bodice is a garment for the upper body.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the upper part of a dress, a garment worn on the torso.

clue.text: Blighter to encourage into pub

indicators.note: the word for encourage goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to egg on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Someone urges a rotten fellow to go into the local.
explanation.walkthrough: EGG (as in 'egg on') goes into BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mildly insulting British words for a wretched or annoying fellow, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Chip in Lorna's computer unit

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so Lorna's gives her surname with possessive S
a bit is the smallest unit of computer data

explanation.surface: A small part has been added to Lorna's computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of a classic English novel; her surname plus 'S gives the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is to contribute one's share, which is what doing your part means.

clue.text: Direct Georgia to dance

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: An order telling Georgia to go out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is a nautical verb meaning to direct the steering of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a long single-file line.

clue.text: Girl serving in clothes shop provided assistance

parts.note: H&M is a high-street clothes retailer
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: A shop assistant in a fashion store has been helping customers.
explanation.walkthrough: H&M is the Swedish chain of clothes shops, common on British high streets; the ampersand is read as AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a female servant or attendant, a young woman in service.

clue.text: Here's an Asian fight raging to remove leader of Islamists

definitions.text: Here's an Asian fight raging to remove leader of Islamists

indicators.note: a raging fight is wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order
one letter is taken away from the fodder before it is rearranged
the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A war-torn Asian land where a struggle rages to oust the Islamist chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (the first letter of Islamists) from the letters of AN ASIAN FIGHT, then rearrange the rest. The whole clue also describes the country, which makes it an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sketches the Asian country where fighting raged to topple the Taliban leadership.

clue.text: The German double barrelled weapon

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a ringer (as in dead ringer) is a double, a lookalike

explanation.surface: A German weapon with two barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double barrelled' looks like one phrase, but 'double' is the wordplay and 'barrelled weapon' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol, a short-barrelled handgun often with two barrels.

clue.text: Gathering of primates -there's one each year

parts.note: a means one
per means each, as in so much per head

explanation.surface: Monkeys meet up once every year.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads A PER Y, one each year.
explanation.definitionFit: An apery is a place where apes are kept, so a collection of these primates.

clue.text: I'll turn up with second to settle score with another person

definitions.text: I'll turn up with second to settle score with another person

indicators.note: the reversed letters and the abbreviation settle inside the musical piece

parts.note: a duet is a musical score written for two performers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: I'll gives its letters I, L, L, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man vows to show up with his second and fight it out with a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a grudge, but in the wordplay it is a musical score for two; 'turn up' reverses I'LL and 'to settle' puts the result plus S inside. The whole clue also describes a duel, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A man fighting a duel shows up with his second, his attendant, to settle a grudge with an opponent.

clue.text: Reason to stop flying

definitions.meaning: the reason or basis for something
to ... an aircraft or pilot is to keep it from flying

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a basis for an argument and also the act of keeping a plane out of the air.

clue.text: Give rage, being out of order

definitions.text: Give rage, being out of order

indicators.note: letters that are out of order are jumbled from their written sequence

explanation.surface: Someone is unreasonably making another person angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out of order' rearranges GIVE RAGE; the whole clue also defines the answer, since to cause rage by misbehaving is to wrong someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to wrong or distress someone, making them resentful and angry.

clue.text: Superman's enemy and artist after a girl

indicators.note: the enemy, the and and the artist all come after the a in the assembled word

parts.note: Lex Luthor is Superman's arch-enemy in the comics
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Superman's foe and a painter are chasing after a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: LEX is Lex Luthor; RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Like Bob Marley, reggae's number one in jamming

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the word for jamming

parts.note: a jammed mechanism is stuck fast or deadlocked

indicators.note: number one of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Bob Marley, reggae's top star, playing in a jam session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jamming' suggests a music session fitting Marley, but here it means stuck: R goes into DEADLOCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley famously wore his hair in long matted locks, the Rastafarian style.

clue.text: Sort of song from Leadbelly disc? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: the extracted letters are read backwards rather than forwards
the letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A tune off a record by the blues singer Leadbelly, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: LLYDI sits across 'Leadbelly disc' and is turned round. Leadbelly was an American folk and blues singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short pastoral poem, a kind of lyric piece once sung.

clue.text: Such as pound in Yorkshire say using metric units

parts.note: Yorkshire pudding is made from a batter, so Yorkshire is an example of batter
grams are metric units of mass

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire recipe measured out in metric weights.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire pudding is a British baked side dish made of batter; 'pound' looks like a weight but is a verb, to strike heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Battering rams are heavy beams used to strike and break down gates, things that hammer repeatedly.

clue.text: What Frankfurt banker used to do is characteristic

definitions.text: What Frankfurt banker used to do
definitions.meaning: before the euro, a German banker would buy and sell Deutsche marks
a distinctive feature by which something is recognised

explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive feature identifies something, while dealing in German currency describes a pre-euro banker's job.

clue.text: Like lad, article, Anglican, repeating the same vowel

definitions.note: a gerund phrase used as a noun: the repeating of one vowel sound

parts.note: as means like
a son is a lad
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A list of words, each repeating one vowel sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a list of words like lad, article and Anglican, all with repeated A sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the echoing of vowel sounds in nearby words, a poetic device.

clue.text: Uncertainty provided penalties to society

parts.note: if means provided, on condition that
fines are money penalties

explanation.surface: Doubt over whether penalties will be imposed on society.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffiness is informal for doubtfulness, the quality of being questionable.

clue.text: Healthy beaches and broads provide intermittent bursts of activity

parts.note: fit means healthy
sands are beaches
broads and tarts are both dated slang for women

explanation.surface: Fit people on beaches with Norfolk Broads boating make for lively bursts of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broads' looks like the Norfolk Broads, the waterways, but it is slang for women; 'and' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fits and starts are irregular spurts of effort, sporadic rather than steady.

clue.text: Face a risky investment, tense

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a risky investment
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Confronting a speculative investment makes one nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: one side of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one side or facet of something, as a face is.

clue.text: Source of comfort King Lear needs

indicators.note: the run of letters is something the two words contain within them

explanation.surface: The old king in Shakespeare's tragedy needs consoling.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'King Lear'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireside or hearth, a warm and cosy spot.

clue.text: Actress torn between 1 Down and 1 Across

indicators.note: the two answers are torn apart, keeping only the letters on either side of where they join

parts.note: the clue points to two other solutions in this grid, the blighter and the top, written one after the other

explanation.surface: An actress cannot choose between two parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answers to 1 Down and 1 Across side by side, then drop BEG from the front and DICE from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star.

clue.text: They have what's necessary to smarten one with trimming

definitions.text: They have what's necessary to smarten one with trimming

indicators.note: they contain the letters needed to spell the fodder, in another arrangement
trimming cuts the end off the word one

explanation.surface: Decorations are what is needed to smarten something up with trim.
explanation.walkthrough: Trimming ONE gives ON; the letters of SMARTEN plus ON are rearranged, and the whole clue describes decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments are decorations, trinkets that make things look smarter.

clue.text: Border patrol?

definitions.meaning: soldiers on patrol walk in step, which is a military walk

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both frontier territory and a regimented military walk, as on a patrol.

clue.text: Reserves mostly gain credit

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to earn is to gain
marks are credit given for work

explanation.surface: Savings in the bank mostly earn interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' looks like a noun but is a verb, to set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Third prize French football team behind Brazil

indicators.note: the French team is placed after the abbreviation

parts.note: BR is the international abbreviation for Brazil
onze is French for eleven, a football team

explanation.surface: France's footballers trail Brazil and finish third.
explanation.walkthrough: A football team has eleven players, so 'French football team' gives ONZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze is the medal awarded for third place.

clue.text: It offers protection when cod steak's gone off

indicators.note: food that has gone off is spoilt, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read as has, adding no letters

explanation.surface: A warning about fish that has spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steak's gone off' means the steak has gone bad; the letters of COD STEAK are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive barrier of upright stakes, a fortification.

clue.text: Danger that is round about

indicators.note: the word that goes round the word for about

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Peril seems to be all around.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a vague warning of danger nearby; 'round about' looks like one phrase, but 'round' is the container signal and 'about' the piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of danger, a menace.
